consensus.basis: Sell-side coverage, carried because it is the measurable proxy for this stage's thesis. Phase 1 measured 1-2 analysts below $1m/day of turnover, 5-7 at $1-5m, 11-13 at $5-25m and 16-19 above, consistently across all three markets. eu_resolve.py ranks the hunt BY this band so the thesis is tested rather than selected on.

history.caveat: Dates are REAL: each row is a results announcement the market's own archive records on that date, and the move is over this stage's own window. Only the UK (Investegate) and Norway (Oslo NewsWeb) reach this state; the other eight markets are estimated.

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against Investegate (RNS mirror) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: sum of disclosed net short positions at or above 0.5% of shares outstanding, as published by the national regulator

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. A name the register was read for and does not name reads 0.0 -- real, but the 0.5% truncation floor rather than a measurement, and below $1m/day of turnover 168 of 190 sampled UK issuers read exactly that. The turnover floor moved from $1m to $200k on 2026-09-19, so this field is how the cost of that move is made visible: eu_resolve.py reports the Spearman split by it, with the count in each arm.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus a reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move, and cut to 0.35 where that history is a cadence estimate rather than observed dates -- measured 2026-09-22, an estimated history lands mostly on ordinary sessions and its median absolute move runs about half an observed one. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved, capped at 0.45 because neither is 25-delta skew and Europe has no margin-balance component to add, and held to 0.15 where the register was read and does not name this issuer -- a truncated zero is not a di…

evidence.text: Non-executive director Guy O'Connor bought 20,000 shares (GBP138k) at 690p on 21 Oct 2026. That is three weeks after the 30 Sep year-end, when the board knew the FY26 outturn and early FY27 order flow, and just before the MAR closed period ahead of the 23 Nov results.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior insider-buy reaction measured. Outlook lines on results days moved the stock +7.0% (FY25 finals, 24 Nov 2025) and +1.3% (FY24 finals).
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it has been public for a month and the stock is up about 25% from 690p since. What remains is the information content for the outlook statement itself. If that were fully in the price, the stock would already sit back above the pre-warning 885p.
evidence.independence: none (the JPM exit below explains the price recovery, not the director's information)

evidence.text: The stock has retraced almost all of the September warning with no company news between: 885p before the warning, 774p on the day, a 660p low on 20 Oct, a run to 936p on 4-12 Nov, and 860p on 20 Nov. The only RNS in that window are the results-date notice and TR-1s. The outlook therefore has to deliver reassurance that is already partly paid for.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two most recent outlook-sensitive releases were both sold: H1 trading update -5.6% (22 Apr 2026) and FY trading update -12.5% (14 Sep 2026). Interims fell -3.6% and -7.4% in 2026 and 2025.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it is partly the free control (-run_up_20d, +23%). It is filed because the size of the retrace sets the bar for the outlook. If the market were demanding nothing, the stock would sit near the 700p post-warning level rather than within 3% of the pre-warning close.
evidence.independence: Kalkine found no company-specific cause for the 4-11 Nov rises (https://kalkine.co.uk/news/technology/cerillion-plc-lsecer-slips-132-what-is-pressuring-the-shares, snippet only, 403 on fetch)

evidence.text: JPMorgan Asset Management cut its stake from 7.53% to 5.30% (9 Oct) and then below 5% (23 Oct 2026). The overhang seller after the warning finished just before the November rally, so less supply hangs over the results day.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior measurement on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the recovery since late October is the visible effect. The residual is the absence of a known large seller into any outlook disappointment.
evidence.independence: Earlier step in the same disposal: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/cerillion--cer/tr-1-notification/9821054 (same holder, so not independent)

evidence.text: No contract-win RNS has been issued since the 8 Jan 2026 Omantel award, so between the 14 Sep warning and 20 Nov no single large deferred order (of the GBP17.3m Sep-2025 follow-on kind, which was RNS'd) has been announced as signed after the year-end.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Large contract RNSs moved the stock up sharply (Omantel +12% intraday on 8 Jan 2026, per AJ Bell).
evidence.why_not_priced: The rally implies the market expects the slipped orders to be signing. The deferred items were licence expansions and upgrades, which Cerillion does not usually announce one by one, so this absence is weak evidence and is sized near zero.

evidence.text: The board raised the interim dividend 15% to 5.5p while H1 adjusted PBT fell 41%. That signals a progressive dividend held through the earnings dip, so a raised final dividend (last year 10.6p) is the likely line on the day.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY25 finals with a +17% total dividend rose 7.0%; the dividend's own share of that move is not separable.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly expected given the dividend history. The final dividend is a new line the market has not seen, and with net cash around GBP36m a step-up is affordable.

evidence.text: Delivery milestones since the warning support FY27 revenue recognition. Telesur's upgrade to Cerillion 26.1 went live on 28 Sep 2026, with a further Self Service phase to follow. The September update had already said Omantel software installation is complete and the UCom transformation is nearing completion.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Operational go-live RNSs have not been measured as movers on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly public. The residual is whether the release confirms the UCom cutover and quantifies FY27 recognition from the back-order book.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Runway restatements have come with prints that moved -9.8% (Q2 2025, strategy reset), +3.6% (Q3 2025) and -0.9% (Q2 2026); never isolated from other news.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the market cap at 2.685 NOK x 391.5m shares is about NOK 1.05bn against an estimated ~USD 65m of cash, so the market already discounts the runway heavily; the dated runway figure itself has not been published since the ruling ('cash runway beyond key value inflection points' was undated). evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ruling itself moved the stock -7.6% on the next session (3.905 to 3.61, 25 to 28 Sep, Yahoo tape); the accounting echo has no precedent on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the ruling and its amount were inside information on 25 Sep and the company said no further payment follows. Only a headline net-loss figure of roughly USD 40m could mislead a screen-reader; the lesson that a known number is worth 0 holds it near zero.
evidence.independence: Q2 report balance-sheet note on Other non-current receivables of USD 33.4m (https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=680771).

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August 2025 strategy reset came with the Q2 2025 report, which moved -9.8%; a cost refocus at this cash level would more likely read as runway-positive.
evidence.why_not_priced: Inference from wording only; no press or forum item picked it up, and the 'About' paragraph still names the tolerance platform, so it may be nothing. If the market expected a refocus, the stock would not be making new lows into the print.

evidence.text: The revenue guide is arithmetically out of reach. H1 reported revenue of EUR 289.5m plus Bloomberg consensus Q3 of EUR 169m means Q4 must reach about EUR 221m, +14% on Q4'25's EUR 193.8m, for even the EUR 680m low end. The acquisitions (Captify and Acardo, Sept 2025) are fully in the base and organic growth ran 3.5% in Q2, so a revenue cut or narrowing to below the low end is the likely guidance outcome. The EBITDA range (Q4 needs about 53.6m against 48.3m in Q4'25) is the swing.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance cut on 14 Aug 2025: -23.4% the next session. Guidance bands narrowed at the Q3 2025 report on 18 Nov 2025: -17.1%. Guide reaffirmed but organic growth missed on 27 Aug 2026: -17.7%. The guide line has moved this stock 17-23% each time, always down.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Inderes already sits below the revenue range and the stock is down 27% since 22 Oct and 40% since the Q2 eve. The preview still expects the company to REITERATE the guide, so the sell side's base case is reiteration. If a cut were fully priced, the preview would model one and the stock would have stopped falling into the print; it fell another 5% in the last five sessions. The EBITDA leg is not priced either way.
evidence.independence: Q4'25 base and FY25 figures come from the issuer's 26 Jan 2026 release (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=bf380afe4b938200cd6fdf161239bb48f&lang=en&src=listed). The consensus comes from the Inderes/Bloomberg table (https://www.inderes.dk/analyst-comments/verve-q326-preview-forste-test-af-den-lovede-h2-acceleration). The arithmetic rests on two documents.

evidence.text: The securitisation expansion that management said in August would be signed 'within the next few weeks' has not been announced three months later. The existing EUR 100m programme was fully drawn at end-Q2. The EUR 500m+50m 2025/2029 FRN printed 82 on Frankfurt on 2026-11-18, down from a ~99 quote. Its terms carry a quarterly maintenance test of NIBD/EBITDA <= 4.50x, with exceptional add-backs capped at 10% of EBITDA, against reported leverage of 4.1x at Q2.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cash flow has been the line the stock punished. Q3 2025 operating cash flow fell 91% and the stock dropped 17.1% on the day (with the guide narrowing). No clean isolated financing reaction exists on record.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the bond at 82 is the credit market saying this, and the equity has fallen with it. What is unpriced is the release's own answer: facility size, tenor, pricing, Q3 cash flow and the compliance figure. Asked what the money buys, the facility funds receivables on a seasonally larger H2, which is ordinary working capital. Its delay therefore reads as lender reluctance rather than a ramp. Signing would flip the sign, hence the wide range. Covenant breach is a tail, not the base case: consensus Q3 EBITDA (~30 reported vs 21.8 in Q3'25) lowers LTM leverage.
evidence.independence: The bond price is a different source: TradingView FWB:SE2384842, last bar 82 on 2026-11-18 (https://www.tradingview.com/symbols/FWB-SE2384842/). This is a single thin Frankfurt print, snippet-grade. A Danish Inderes forum post of 16.11.2026 notes the bond has fallen during the year.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 prelim, which showed an organic rebound: -4.0% (an intraday release, so the move is mixed). Q1 2026 'solid organic growth': +2.5%. Good reported-quarter lines have earned only small gains here.
evidence.why_not_priced: Verve fell through the peers' beats (Magnite 4 Nov, PubMatic ~10 Nov), so the read-through has not reached this price. Had it, VER would have tracked the peers' rallies. This is a proxy, though: Inderes expects Verve to lag both peer groups and Verve's organic growth trailed peers in Q2, so it is sized small.

evidence.text: CEO Remco Westermann (via Bodhivas GmbH) bought roughly 360k shares (~EUR 0.4m) on 19-23 Oct 2026. Q3 had closed by then, and the window ended just before the 30-day MAR closed period. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction to insider buying for this name. The stock fell 27% after these purchases.
evidence.why_not_priced: The purchases are public, but the stock has since fallen 27% to SEK 8.64, below his SEK 11.6-11.8 cost. So the market has priced a deterioration the CEO did not see at the time, or priced past the information. It is an inference about Q3 rather than a number, and it is small relative to his holding, so it is sized small.
